youtube.title: WEDNSDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Jaspreet Boparai and Don Nicolson are joined by Mark Hooper, Bryce McKenzie and Owen Jennings to examine the future of New Zealand’s primary sector, from the Paris Agreement and emissions policy to resource management, biodiversity credits, GE and free trade. The discussion ultimately turns to property rights, bureaucratic overreach and the importance of strategic voting ahead of the election. youtube.title: MAKI HERBERT
youtube.summary: Maki Herbert, co-leader of the Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party and its Te Tai Tokerau candidate, joins Paul Brennan to discuss the party’s 30-year campaign for cannabis legalisation. They cover the 2020 referendum, medicinal cannabis and roadside THC testing, the potential economic and employment opportunities of a legal cannabis and hemp industry, drug-law reform and Māori communities and why Maki believes prohibition has failed. youtube.title: SHANE JONES
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Shane Jones, Deputy Leader of NZ First, about the election campaign, polls, NZ First’s candidate list and concerns over growing state power. They discuss beneficiary drug testing, fuel security, domestic energy and shipping capacity, economic sovereignty and the protection of New Zealand’s coastal resources, with Shane arguing for stronger national independence and greater safeguards for essential services. youtube.title: HANNAH TAMAKI
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Hannah Tamaki, leader of Vision New Zealand and pastor at Destiny Church, about her decision to contest Papakura after previously standing in Māori electorates. Hannah outlines Vision New Zealand’s campaign priorities, including opposition to the New Zealand–India free trade agreement, immigration concerns, protecting New Zealand industries and her vision for a unified national identity. youtube.title: GRAEME EDGELER
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with constitutional and electoral law expert Graeme Edgeler about how the MMP overhang could influence New Zealand’s election result and coalition options. They examine strategic voting, the Māori electorates’ role in creating an overhang, possible changes to electoral rules and whether a government shaped by extra electorate seats would still be legitimate.
